# requirements-ci.txt - the hashed LOCK that GitHub Actions installs, and nothing
# else does. Used by .github/workflows/daily.yml and add-product.yml as:
#     pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-ci.txt
#
# Why (board review 2026-09-21): the hourly build used to install whatever
# yfinance / pandas / numpy release PyPI served that hour, in the job that also
# builds the data.json the bot trades on. Every package below is pinned with ==
# and carries EVERY sha256 PyPI lists for that exact version (all platforms, so
# any wheel pip picks matches). A new or re-uploaded release can therefore not
# reach CI without a commit to this file, and a file whose hash does not match
# stops "Install deps" before any of it runs.
#
# The set is exactly what the runner resolved from requirements.txt on
# 2026-09-21 (daily.yml run 35643856094: CPython 3.12.14, ubuntu-24.04 x86_64),
# taken from that log's "Successfully installed" line, with the hashes from the
# PyPI JSON API. It is resolved for Python 3.12 on Linux only (numpy 2.5.3 needs
# >= 3.12), which is why it is a separate file: requirements.txt stays the short
# human-readable list that the desktop and the VM's python3.11 test export use.
#
# How to bump (e.g. Yahoo changes something and only a newer yfinance works):
#   1. If a floor must move, edit requirements.txt first.
#   2. On Linux with Python 3.12 (WSL, a codespace or a container), in a venv:
#          pip install pip-tools
#          pip-compile --generate-hashes --output-file requirements-ci.txt requirements.txt
#      Add  --upgrade-package yfinance  to move one package and keep the other
#      pins; without it pip-compile keeps every pin that still fits. It writes
#      all the hashes of each chosen version, like this file, but replaces this
#      header - paste the header back.
#   3. Or by hand: change the == line, and replace its --hash lines with every
#      "sha256" under "urls" in https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json.
#      If the new version needs a package or version not pinned here, pip stops
#      with "Hashes are required in --require-hashes mode" or a conflict - add
#      or bump that one the same way.
#   4. Read the diff: every changed line is new third-party code that runs in
#      CI. The next push to main runs the build; a bad pin or hash fails
#      "Install deps" loudly and the last good dashboard stays up.
#
beautifulsoup4==4.15.0 \

    --hash=sha256:d6f88de62e1d4e38ecb1077eb9724cd0eff29d2a08ca16a401e9b9e93f117cf9
